terms: Sovereignty: technical and contractual access sufficient to independently verify or intervene on an AI system without the vendor's ongoing discretionary cooperation; this is distinct from territorial sovereignty (3.1).
Sovereignty and control are orthogonal: sovereignty is an access condition, control is a protocol (3.1).
Four-layer typology (3.1): data, model, infrastructure and interaction sovereignty. Interaction sovereignty covers prompts, outputs, tool calls, logs, traces and pre-execution intervention points.
Bounded sovereignty: partial access across the four layers (Abstract, 8).
Control tax: the operational and financial cost of integrating control into AI pipelines, following Terekhov et al. 2025 (3.1).
Two-layer control problem (1.2): Layer 1 is protocol effectiveness given access; Layer 2 is access feasibility.

Sovereignty discount cost: the extra expenditure, delay, residual risk or usefulness loss needed to approximate a protocol whose required access is missing. Realised control tax = instrumented-control cost + sovereignty discount cost, and the discount is not always finite (3.3).

Sovereignty-discount proxy: the minimum cost to reach a target failure rate under bounded access, minus the minimum cost under full instrumentation. A strict variant also requires ≥75% task success (4.3).
Experimental access factors (4.2): I/O logs, tool-call logs, gateway, trace access, model-version control, vendor support and tool scope, combined into 20 fractional-factorial access profiles.
Diagnosis success is evidence-based: a failure counts as diagnosable only if the evidence available under the access profile is enough to reconstruct it (4.3).
Catastrophic-action classes C1–C4 (4.1, 6.1): incorrect hold or release, systematic mis-triage, sensitive-data exposure, and settlement-critical action.
Synthetic agents: honest, careless and stealthy access-aware (4.2).
